front: TC025: What is the minimum viable move?
back: The next time you present work that involved others, name at least one contributor specifically before you present it.

front: TC025: What is the core sequence?
back: Name who contributed -> Name what they did -> Do not be vague.

front: TC025: What is the field tip?
back: Credit given in the big room counts double; credit given vaguely counts for nothing.

front: TC025: What is the strong version of: Vague: 'A great team effort'?
back: [Name] built the analysis. [Name] caught the error. I pulled it together.

front: TC025: What is the strong version of: Taking full credit for collaborative work?
back: Name each person's specific contribution before presenting the work.

front: TC025: What is the strong version of: Over-crediting: spreading it so thin no one seems particularly important?
back: Name the two or three people whose contribution was most essential. Be specific.

front: TC025: What is better than: 'Massive team effort, everyone was amazing.'?
back: '[Name] built the model, [Name] found the flaw, and I pulled the story together.'

front: TC025: What is better than: '...oh, and thanks to the team, obviously.' — as the meeting ends?
back: Name contributors in the opening, before the content — where the attention is.

front: TC025: What is better than: Warm words one-to-one, silence in the rooms that matter?
back: 'I want this room to know: section three is entirely [Name]'s work.'

front: TC025: What are signs it is working?
back: Team members feel seen and valued. You are trusted more by senior stakeholders, not less. A culture of recognition spreads. You feel clean about how you represent your work.

front: TC025: When should you avoid this technique?
back: When your individual contribution needs to be visible for legitimate reasons — e.g. a performance review where your specific work must be legible. When sharing credit for something that went wrong — ownership of failure is different from shared credit for success.

front: TC025: What is the best recovery line?
back: 'I presented that as mine and it was ours. Let me correct the record.'
